heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Prusament PC Blend reliably out of the box using its stock hardened steel nozzle and enclosed chamber. Capping volumetric throughput to 12 mm³/s ensures robust layer bonding at safe print speeds up to 143 mm/s.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with glue stick or liquid glue applied as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Filament Max Volumetric Speed to 12 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer to prevent high-speed underextrusion.
Disable the Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan completely (0%) to prevent localized drafts and edge curling.
Set Bed Temperature to 110°C and preheat the chamber by running the bed for 15-20 minutes before initiating the print.
Enable an outer brim with a 5 mm width and a 0.1 mm brim-object gap to anchor sharp corners firmly.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: High thermal shrinkage stress combined with insufficient chamber temperature or lack of release barrier.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply Bambu Liquid Glue or PVP glue stick on the Textured PEI plate, keep the door and top lid sealed, and pre-heat the bed at 110°C for 20 minutes.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Layer separation and brittle inter-layer bonding
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speeds chilling the extruded PC bead below its glass transition temperature prematurely.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Lower part cooling fan speeds to 0% min and 20% max, turn off the aux fan, and raise nozzle temperature to 275°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in the hygroscopic polycarbonate matrix causing steam cavitation in the hotend.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool in an active filament dryer or the X1C chamber drying mode at 75°C for at least 8 to 12 hours before printing.

faq.question: Do I need an adhesive on the Textured PEI plate when printing Prusament PC Blend?
faq.answer: Yes, an adhesive like glue stick or liquid glue is mandatory as a sacrificial release agent to prevent the polycarbonate from permanently bonding and ripping off the PEI coating.

faq.question: Should the Bambu Lab X1C door or top lid be left open when printing PC?
faq.answer: No, the chamber must remain fully closed during the entire print job to trap ambient heat and avoid thermal contraction warping.

faq.question: Can Prusament PC Blend be used in the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, standard Prusament spools fit the AMS, but ensure the desiccant packs are fresh because PC absorbs ambient moisture very rapidly.

faq.question: Why is the printing speed restricted to 143 mm/s?
faq.answer: At a 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm line width, 143 mm/s corresponds to the safe 12 mm³/s maximum volumetric limit of the stock hotend to ensure complete plasticization.
